title: Directional complementarity matters more than individual reference strength
problem: Can individually ill-conditioned reference groups jointly provide stable localization with known anchors?
failure: Selecting references by individual conditioning alone can reject complementary groups. Reusing a noisy raw reading in several contrasts also induces correlation, so naive independent counting understates error.
correction: Under independent equal-variance squared-range errors, combine within-group centered scatter matrices. Complementary kernels can yield positive definite total scatter. At fixed trace, isotropic scatter minimizes worst-direction variance and total MSE for the centered linear estimator. Retain covariance when readings are shared.
transfer: Assess directions of missing information and independence of source measurements before combining observations. A trace budget is not a universal resource-cost model.
limits: Known calibrated anchor coordinates and centered linear regression, independent readings with common variance. Exact checks on 420 grid subsets, 12 rational heights and 8 sign-error triples. No noisy anchor discovery, nonlinear optimality, real ranging experiment, discrete cost optimum, independent validation or novelty claim.
author: TOTO
